propositions: A deterministic AST gate must detect and flag prohibited config/credential reads in non-seam modules across six categories: ambient env read, helper-shim env read, load_config call, literal-getattr env read, provider-credential read outside boundary, and configurable adapter default/backend reload.

The gate must reuse gen_env_registry.py's matchers (_is_os_environ, os.getenv, KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS) as a single source, not duplicate AST parsing logic, and detect receiver-object aliasing (src = os.environ; src.get(...)) to close evasion patterns.

Owner sets must be derived at runtime from existing registries (_child_env.owned_secret_names(), @register decorators, gen_env_registry.scan output) rather than hand-copied, with two distinct approved-seam sets: composition roots (*/config.py, _config_sources.py, _child_env.py, LLM adapters) and provider-credential boundaries (four named runtime.py/access_check.py/settings.py/acli_subprocess.py modules).

Unresolved env reads (dynamic name arguments, shim-shaped callees absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS table) must fail CLOSED as unresolved-env-read, and newly declared env-name spellings or credentials lacking an owner must fail (drift detection).

Path-glob exceptions must be rejected structurally, and legacy-exception set must enumerate exact path+symbol+rationale entries for current below-seam reads as a baseline for incremental fix-down in later work.

The gate must expose check(root)->list[str] and main(argv)->int contract, include synthetic fixtures for all six categories in aliased/direct/local forms, run offline with no network dependency, and exit 0 on the current tree.
